Staged Releases: Levels will open in stages and remain accessible until the competition ends. Hints Along the Way: Hints will be released to help participants progress. No Elimination: Participants can continue solving challenges throughout the competition period. Who Can Participate? Recognition for outstanding performance. About the Organisers IEEE Student Branch and IET On Campus at Birla Institute of Technology, Mesra, Ranchi, are student-run campus chapters of two leading engineering societies. Since 2019, we have been organising Capture The Flag competitions, technical events, and hands-on workshops covering Linux, Git, Python, web development, and more. With CICADA 2026, we aim to bring an engaging, month-long puzzle-solving experience to participants across India. Important Dates Competition Starts: 10 December 2026 Competition Ends: 10 January 2027 Mode: Completely Online Get ready to decode, investigate, collaborate, and uncover what lies beyond the next clue. title: ELU Build
description: About ELUBuild ELUBuild is the flagship solo product-building challenge by EduLinkUp . Over the course of the buildathon, individual builders pitch innovative software ideas, and once approved, build, document, and ship real-world SaaS applications from the ground up. The mission of ELUBuild is to discover and empower solo builders to create sustainable, user-ready digital products. Exceptional projects will be selected for integration into the ELU Store platform, with opportunities for direct deployment, hosting, and potential publishing on the Google Play Store on behalf of EduLinkUp. The Complete Event Flow ELUBuild runs across clear, structured phases: Registration & Track Exploration: Register via the EduLinkUp mobile app. Review the announced tracks and loose problem statement suggestions provided by EduLinkUp. These serve as inspiration-participants are completely free to think beyond these suggestions and tackle any authentic, high-impact problem within the domain. Use this phase to brainstorm, validate needs, and prepare your pitch before the idea portal opens. Idea Submission Phase: When the idea window opens, submit your idea proposal (project name, problem statement, target users, proposed solution, anticipated tech stack, solo buildability feasibility, and an explanatory video link). You can submit anytime while the window is active. Continuous Review & Approval: The EduLinkUp team reviews submissions on a rolling basis. Ideas can be approved at any time while the window is open. Share Your Vision: Once your idea is approved, you can (and are encouraged to) publish your explanatory pitch video on social media. Social Media Engagement Leaderboard (Active in Idea & Build Phases): A dedicated engagement leaderboard tracks reach, quality, and engagement of participants' social media posts across both the Idea Phase and the Building Phase . Compelling explanations, progress updates, and demos that resonate with the community rank higher. Idea Phase Closure, Review & Stage 1 Certification: The idea submission portal closes at 11:59 PM IST on the deadline day. The final review round is completed, and results are officially released to all participants. Stage 1 Certification: All builders whose ideas are approved receive official Stage 1 ELUBuild recognition and advance to the building phase. Building Phase (Next.js + Supabase): Building takes place inside the edulinkup-interns GitHub organisation. Shortlisted builders create their public repository under edulinkup-interns . Mandatory Tech Stack: Projects must be built using Next.js and Supabase , with authentication integrated via EduLinkUp OAuth ( @edulinkup/auth SDK). Detailed step by step instructions/guide of connecting your site with EduLinkUp OAuth will be shared before the building phase. Weekly Social Updates: Builders must share at least one weekly progress update on social media (e.g., #buildinpublic , feature demos, architecture highlights, or lessons learned). Engaging, authentic content helps you climb the Social Leaderboard. Repository Commits & Commit Quality Leaderboard: Steady, consistent development through the build window is tracked on a dedicated Commit Leaderboard . Quality & Consistency Over Raw Volume: Scoring evaluates steady engineering rhythm, meaningful commit messages, and genuine code evolution-not artificial commit spamming or scripts. Manual Audits: Code and repository activity will be regularly inspected manually. Use of commit bots, artificial commit scripts, or bulk dumping pre-existing code on the final day will lead to immediate disqualification . Final Submission & Judging: Submit your GitHub repository (under edulinkup-interns ), a deployed live demo URL, and a comprehensive product walkthrough video. Independent evaluations determine top ranks (Winner / Top 1, Top 3, Top 5, Top 7, and All participants). title: Anveshak: Open-World Object Detection for Remote Sensing
description: About Anveshak: Open-World Object Detection for Remote Sensing is a national computer vision competition by Techfest, IIT Bombay. Earth-observation systems support disaster response, maritime and defence surveillance, urban planning, agriculture, and climate monitoring, yet three problems limit them in practice: imagery always contains unknown objects the taxonomy does not cover, new classes arrive gradually with only a few examples, and learning new categories can quietly degrade performance on old ones. Teams build one remote sensing detector that handles all three while keeping the same model throughout, trained entirely from random initialisation with no pretrained weights of any kind. Take on the challenge at Techfest, IIT Bombay, Asia's largest science and technology festival. Structure The competition has an online Round 1, an on-site Round 2, and an on-site Finale at Techfest, IIT Bombay. Eligibility: Open to all students with a valid ID from their educational institution. Cross-institutional teams are encouraged. Team size: Maximum 4 members per team. The Challenge: Design and train one remote sensing detector that learns in two rounds and keeps the same model throughout. It must detect 40 known classes in Round 1, flag unknown objects as unknown rather than forcing them into known classes, learn 10 new classes from a small number of images each without forgetting the base classes, and then learn 10 fresh classes in Round 2 while still flagging unknowns. Key constraints: Every model is trained from random initialisation, with no ImageNet, COCO, self-supervised (e.g. DINOv2), remote sensing, or other pretrained weights. Open-source detection frameworks are allowed with pretrained-weight loading switched off; open-vocabulary models are not permitted as the detector. The model must remain one lineage: train on Set A, continue on Set B, then continue into Round 2, with the same architecture and no retraining from scratch or replacement. Round 1 - Online Teams receive Dataset A, Dataset B, unlabelled Round 1 test images, the class list, and a validator script. They train on Dataset A first, then continue on Dataset B with the same model; training images may contain unlabelled objects of unknown classes. Teams submit one Google Drive folder containing a predictions CSV for the Round 1 test images, the Round 1 checkpoint (weights after Set A then Set B), training and inference code with a README, and a 5-7 slide methodology PPT (problem understanding, methodology, first implementation, Round 2 plan, and team roles). Screening is on the OE-Score, computed on the full Round 1 test set, plus checkpoint reproduction: organisers re-run the checkpoint on the Round 1 test images and its predictions must match the submitted CSV within tolerance. The PPT is also checked for completeness. Round 2 - On-site, 16th December 2026 Held at Techfest, IIT Bombay. The Round 2 dataset and unlabelled test images are released at the start of the Round 2 window. Teams learn 10 fresh classes from a small number of images, starting from their verified Round 1 checkpoint (no other starting weights are permitted), without forgetting earlier classes and while still flagging unknowns. Round 2 training images may contain unlabelled objects of base, few-shot, and unknown classes. Teams train on the Round 2 dataset plus data released in earlier rounds only. The window closes at a fixed time to be announced on the day; teams may submit at any point within the window. The deliverable is a predictions CSV for the Round 2 test images. Outcome: shortlisting for the Finale. Finale - On-site, 17th December 2026 Organisers re-run inference for each shortlisted team on the Round 2 test images. Shortlisted teams submit code, weights, and a two-page technical note, present their approach to the panel, and answer questions. Outcome: final ranking. Scoring Primary score is the OE-Score = 100 x 2 x mAP_K x U-F1 / (mAP_K + U-F1), built from known-class detection (mAP_K) and unknown-object handling (U-F1, the harmonic mean of unknown recall and precision). All matching uses IoU 0.5. Ranking is by OE-Score on the full test set; tie-breaks in both rounds are higher mAP_K, then higher U-F1, then earlier submission time. Timeline Registration closes - 30th November 2026, 11:59 PM Round 1 submission deadline - 30th November 2026, 11:59 PM Round 1 results announcement - 3rd December 2026 Round 2 (On-site) - 16th December 2026 Finale (On-site) - 17th December 2026 Rewards and Prizes INR 1,50,000 for the top 3 winners. Certificates for all participants who qualify for Round 2

description: Overview Five editions. Pass the baton, build the future. WebnD, the Web and Design Society of IIT Bhubaneswar, is back with the fifth edition of its flagship hackathon. Builders, dreamers and problem-solvers from across India will battle it out in two electrifying tracks: Web2 and Web3 .  PPI Opportunities Top performers in the Web2 tracks get a shot at Pre-Placement Interview (PPI) opportunities from CSM Technologies. Build something great and it could land you more than a trophy. Who Can Join the Relay Open to everyone, whatever your discipline, degree or background Squad up in teams of 2 to 4 members Teammates can come from different colleges, schools or organisations Teams lock the moment you register, with no swaps and no substitutions. Pick your dream team wisely. Round 1: The Ideathon and Prototyping (Online) Problem statements for both tracks drop for all registered teams. Pitch your best idea in one PPT using the provided template by December 12 . Want to stand out? Attach a working prototype and score bonus points. The most promising teams will be shortlisted and invited to the main arena. Round 2: The Hackathon (On-site at IIT Bhubaneswar) Shortlisted teams must report on campus by January 15 . Miss the check-in and you are out of the race. Get 30 hours of non-stop building, with power and internet on us throughout. Take the stage and pitch live to the judges: your idea , your product and your business strategy . Fair play matters. Pre-existing projects are allowed only if disclosed in advance, and undisclosed ones will be disqualified. The Finale Celebrate the final lap at a networking lunch with fellow participants, judges, sponsors and speakers. Great code gets you here, great connections take you further.
